name: Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan
description: Seventeen archaeological sites across southern Hokkaido and northern Honshu's Tohoku region preserve traces of the Jomon, who settled in villages for roughly 10,000 years without farming, living by hunting, fishing and gathering. Visitors can see ritual earthworks, stone circles over 50 metres wide, and replicas of the famous goggle-eyed clay figurines. Together they show how an early settled society lived and worshipped.
